lead.claim: Capacity gains do not guarantee real-world upper limb use after stroke.
lead.context: Why this matters: This study looked at how upper limb capacity and real-world use change after stroke over six months.

supporting.claim: Consider low-load BFR-RT for sarcopenia if high-load training is difficult.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This exploratory RCT investigated low-load BFR-RT for sarcopenia and mild cognitive impairment in oldest-old adults.

supporting.claim: Incorporate chair-based exercise for AECOPD patients during hospitalization.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This randomized controlled trial evaluated chair-based exercise for patients with acute exacerbation of COPD.

supporting.claim: Rehab protocols for medial meniscus repair need more active training details.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This scoping review examined published rehabilitation protocols for medial meniscus posterior root repair.

supporting.claim: Cervical lidocaine injections offer modest, short-term relief for cervicogenic dizziness.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This randomized, sham-controlled trial assessed low-dose cervical paraspinal lidocaine injections for cervicogenic dizziness.
